name: grid-wave
title: Grid Wave
description: A wave crosses the frame (outward from the centre, or left, right, up or down) and lifts the picture into a grid of solid tiles with a gap between them, tinted and shaded as they rise, then sets them down carrying the next scene. Runs its WebGL shader over two built-in panels (a stat and a bar chart, then a render queue; text and colours from variables), not over the host's scenes: 60 frames of the first panel, a 36-frame transition, then the second panel. To use it between your own scenes, copy the shader into your composition and feed it your two frames as textures.
useWhen: A product or interface demo needs a cut with craft: the frame is handled as a surface rather than blended away.
The moment can afford well over a second; the wave has to travel far enough to read as a wave.
The two scenes are both structured and graphic, so the grid reads as a deliberate device.
avoidWhen: The cut needs to be quick or invisible: use zoom-blur.
You want the frame to come apart into matter rather than be handled as tiles: use particle-dissolve.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Tile size
variables.description: Width of one tile. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Wave width
variables.description: Width of the wave front, as a share of the frame.

variables.label: Lift
variables.description: How far tiles rise as the wave passes.

variables.label: Tint
variables.description: Colour the rising tiles pick up.

variables.label: Direction
variables.description: Where the wave starts and which way it travels.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Tiles are large and flat; 0.5 matches 1 in the stills and keeps the nine-tile search cheap.
